title: Vowel Block
text: To solve this problem, treat the vowels (o, u, a, i) as a single entity or "block" since they must form a string.

title: Number of Consonants
text: After treating the vowels as a single block, you have to arrange the consonants and the "vowel block". How many total elements are there?

title: Using the Arrangement Formula
text: Because order matters, use an arrangement formula. Treat the vowel block as one object along with the consonants.

title: Arrangement Formula
text: For $$n$$ objects with repeated items, the number of distinct arrangements is n!/(r_1!*r_2!*...). Here, arrange the $$6$$ objects using 6!/2!.

title: Repetition
text: Only one consonant is repeated. How many times does it occur? Its factorial will be in the denominator of the arrangement formula.

title: Number of Vowels
text: How many vowels are in the word?

title: Finding the answer
text: Arrange the $$6$$ objects using 6!/2!, then multiply by 4! for the possible arrangements of the four vowels within the vowel block.
